analysis.title: US Market Intelligence - Morning Briefing (November 16, 2026)
key_insights: JPM Market Intel is tactically bullish on US equities into year-end. It argues positioning is cleaner, entry points are better, and the AI build-out may be slower but demand remains strong. Inflation is the main risk, which it sees as an early-2027 problem because a 50bp Fed hike in December is considered highly unlikely.

SPX rose 3.6% last week, ending a 4-week losing streak that cost 5.3%, and is back at the bottom of its Aug-Oct trading range. NVDA fell 12.8% on the week and is down 34.6% over 6 weeks, while the SOX gained 9.2% and memory gained 7.9%. This happened as hawkish inflation data and Fedspeak pushed yields up at the fastest pace in several years.

Bull case for the week has four parts. (i) NVDA earnings need to reiterate capex and support for existing financing deals, and give clarity on leadership given a push to bring Huang back. NVDA options flows have moved from downside protection to playing for upside surprises. (ii) Capital markets events need to trade well to support the expected ECM/DCM/M&A wave before the next Congress is seated on Jan 3. (iii) The JPM APAC Tech Conference in Hong Kong (about 250 firms including Samsung, SK Hynix, TSMC) could let hedge funds, who sold for 6 straight weeks, stabilize the AI trade. (iv) An in-line or stronger Retail Sales print would shift flows back toward Beta and Cyclicals.

Bear case has four parts. (i) AI/Tech takes another leg lower if NVDA fails to reassure on AI financing, capital markets events are delayed, or negative pre-announcements come out of the APAC conference. (ii) Retail dip-buyers and buybacks could step back if Tech falls again. (iii) A hotter Retail Sales print plus continued hawkish Fedspeak, with 17 Fed speakers this week and some discussing 50bp, could challenge the current pricing of 4 hikes including December. (iv) Aggregate US positioning is only about the 20th percentile and global Semis exposure is about the 80th percentile, so there has been no definitive positioning purge.

Monetization Menu (Nov 16) favors moving back toward Tech, with primary exposure to Mag7 and options to play a rebound in AI themes. Outside Tech it prefers Cyclicals over Defensives and continues to like Europe for Cyclical/Value exposure, though a stronger USD could temper it. The call is patient: the market is expected to wait for earnings, capital markets events and the APAC conference before moving.

Rates sold off sharply last week. The 2Y yield rose 34bp, its largest weekly move in over 2 years, and the 10Y rose 28bp, the largest since the week after Liberation Day. The MOVE index rose 6.3 vols, but higher bond vol has not led to the usual equity declines in recent weeks.

Jay Barry sees the market pricing hikes in Dec, Jan and 2 more by YE27, with a high bar for 50bp in Dec or Jan. He prefers 2s/5s flatteners as a hedge against a more hawkish Fed, which would also invert the money market curve. His forecast has the 10Y holding near 5.15% for a month and falling to 5.05% at year-end, with the 2Y moving from about 4.90% to 4.70% and the curve re-steepening into 27H1.

Meera Chandan is bullish on the Dollar. She sees hawkish Fed repricing as the dominant driver, with falling energy prices a mild headwind. She notes the Dollar is currently more sensitive to Fed pricing than to oil, and that US exceptionalism in growth and yields is not being reflected in equities.

FactSet earnings update with 91% of the SPX reported: blended revenue growth is 14.4% and blended EPS growth is 31.9%, versus pre-season expectations of 12.4% and 29.6%. All 11 sectors have positive revenue and earnings growth, which has happened once before (21Q2). Revenue surprises are above average and earnings surprises below average. Beats are not rewarded and misses are not punished. NTM P/E is 18.3x, below the 5-year and 10-year averages.

Macro data has been strong (Flash PMIs, ISM, NFP) alongside a hot CPI. Friday's PPI cut JPM's PCE tracking estimate to 0.295% MoM, about 3.2% YoY. Feroli expects Retail Sales this week at 0.0% MoM headline and +0.3% ex-autos, with the tax-stimulus boost fading and high gas prices weighing. US Market Intel argues consumption levels remain high because of large consumer cash balances and full employment.

Positioning Intelligence weekly wrap asks whether the Semis sell-off is over. HF selling in US Semis ran 6 straight weeks, the longest streak on record, and HF net exposure is down 67% from its year-to-date high. A bounce is possible given the combined positioning and price z-score near -3z, but history suggests it may not be robust unless HFs turn more bullish. Gross flows and HF performance showed signs of stabilization.

Regional positioning: Europe has rebounded and relative EU positioning versus US is back to neutral. Japan was broadly sold, with HF flows at -1.4z WoW and combined Japan positioning at the 24th percentile since 2015.

Consumer sector: Matt Boss reports Chase card data showing 3Q discretionary spending +5.9%, accelerating from 2Q at +5.3%, with October moderating to +5.4%. He lowers 26Q3 estimates across Apparel and Footwear, sees ROST, FIVE, VSXY, DG, OLLI and URBN as relatively insulated, and sees holiday opportunities in TPR, RL, REF and BOOT.

Chris Horvers raises SSS estimates for HD, LOW and TGT above consensus and holds WMT slightly below consensus. His setup views: WMT near-term muted after the stock run, TGT tricky into the print and dependent on whether October is the anomaly or the trend, and HD/LOW relatively full but attractive into the print.

JPM FICC weekly: fixed income desks recommend 2s/5s flatteners, unwinding 2s/3s swap spread curve steepeners and soft-bearish exposure in 30Y tails. They also recommend short weighted TY calendar spreads for the Z6/H7 roll because asset manager longs are at historic highs. They forecast record US IG gross issuance of $2.1tr in 2027, including $450bn of AI-related supply, and say asset managers rather than insurers have done most of the hyperscaler bond buying.

Dubravko reiterates a YE26 SPX target of 8,000 and trades: long 12M Momentum versus short 3M Momentum, Low Vol less compelling, AI Upstream attractive after the positioning flush, and Consumer Cyclicals challenged by affordability but with longer-term value in Apparel, Restaurants and Retail versus Energy.
